01-hook.text: One mole is leaking a company's documents. An AI head of security gets one accusation. This is Canary Lab: Gemini plays, explains and attacks its own benchmark.

02-problem.text: Agents now make irreversible calls under uncertainty. Before you ship one, you pick a model and how hard it thinks. One benchmark number can't tell you where they fail, whether more thinking would help, or whether the score can be gamed.

03-ladder.text: So Gemini plays. Five models, up to four thinking levels, one hundred fifty-seven paired episodes. On hard, n equals eight: ninety-two percent, interval seventy-six to one hundred thirteen, at medium, and one hundred two percent, interval eighty-four to one hundred twenty-nine, at high. Gemini three point six Flash, requested as three point five, is within those intervals of the solver, sixteen of sixteen correct, at thirty-four to thirty-nine cents per episode versus one dollar thirty for Gemini four Carbon on high thinking.

04-atlas.text: Then Gemini reads. All 153 trajectories in one cached context, without our labels. Blind, it recovered 3 of 5 failure modes our code defines and named 2 new ones. Coverage is still weak: the steps it cites hold 21 percent of all regret.

05-swarm.text: Then Gemini attacks. One hundred attacks in four waves, most with our whole codebase in context. Zero verified exploits. To test the detector, we reopened a closed hole: it caught four of four.

06-innovative.text: That is the innovation: a benchmark that measures, explains and audits itself. Across two hundred ninety-five episodes, every lost point is tagged to a decision, with nothing unexplained.

07-essential.text: Three Gemini features make this possible. Thinking level is the ladder's knob. Thought signatures keep reasoning across tool calls. The explicit cache served 85 percent of input tokens, and the whole programme cost 222 dollars at list price. TTS and Live only narrate.

08-close.text: Recorded Gemini runs replay offline. Make lab replay. No key needed.
